newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Merukh says unaffected by Bre-X deal.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Merukh says unaffected by Bre-X deal.

text.p: Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh said on Tuesday he would continue to pursue his claim for a 40-percent stake in the Busang gold find, which is majority owned by Bre-X Minerals Ltd of Canada.
Merukh told Reuters that a Bre-X deal with a company controlled by President Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto would not affect his claim to a part of the spectacular find in Kalimantan.
"There's no change in my position. I will pursue my claim for 40 percent (of Busang)," he said.
Merukh said the deal between Bre-X and Sigit's PT Panutan Duta "is news to me", but added that it was positive because it meant another Indonesian was involved in the property.
"My 40 percent is intact. They (Bre-X and Sigit) can share the rest," he said.

Bre-X announced on Monday that PT Panutan would receive a 10-percent interest in the richest parts of the Busang find, which has been under a cloud following an ownership dispute between Merukh and Bre-X.
